plan: Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid my true value of $3. This means bidding exactly $3 minimizes my risk of losing money. Since values are randomly drawn and independent each round, there's no historical information to adjust my strategy. By bidding my true value, I avoid overpaying if I win and maximize my chances of winning at a fair price relative to my personal valuation.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $24. In a single-round auction with no repeated interactions, bidding my true value minimizes the risk of overbidding and losing money. Since the values are independently drawn and this is a one-time game, strategic deception offers no clear advantage. I will bid my exact private value to optimize potential profit.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly my true value ($11) is the dominant strategy in a second-price sealed-bid auction. Since values are independently and randomly drawn each round, there's no strategic advantage to bidding above or below my true value. I want to maximize my potential profit by winning if my value is highest, while minimizing overpayment. Bidding $11 ensures I win if my value is highest and pays only the second-highest bid.
